SeasonRecap:
David Boylston's 1999 Saints were defending SCISA Class AA champions, but the fall became a rebuild around a much younger roster. The preseason preview listed only five returning starters and 20 first-year players, with seniors Michael Paton, Evan Aldrich, Andy Moreland and Joseph Hinely carrying the bridge from the 1998 title team.

The opening two weeks showed the cost of that turnover. Byrnes Academy ended St. Andrew's 11-game winning streak with a 6-0 win, holding the Saints to 101 total yards, and Dorchester followed with a 26-3 result despite Matt Mahany's first-quarter field goal. St. Andrew's answered at Thomas Heyward, where Paton ran for 219 yards and Evan Aldrich hit Ryan Stratz for a 41-yard fourth-quarter touchdown in a 13-6 win.

Paton's surge became the season's center. He ran for 240 yards and five touchdowns against Colleton Prep, then set a school single-game rushing record with 259 yards and four touchdowns in a 28-21 upset at Sea Island. By the Nov. 10 Coastal Empire leaders, Paton had 1,784 rushing yards and 20 rushing touchdowns through the regular season, while Aldrich had thrown for 656 yards and four scores.

The Saints stayed in the SCISA AA playoff race despite midseason losses to Williamsburg, Calhoun and Hilton Head Prep. A scoreboard-only Patrick Henry result and the rescheduled Thomas Sumter game completed the regular season, with Paton running for 260 yards and five touchdowns against Thomas Sumter while Zach Hillard returned an interception for a score and Matt Hunt broke the school tackles record. St. Andrew's finished 5-6 after a 27-22 playoff loss at Williamsburg, where Paton scored rushing and receiving touchdowns and Lee Stubbs returned a fumble 83 yards.

The winter archive added the postseason coda. Michael Paton and Evan Aldrich represented St. Andrew's in the SCISA North-South All-Star Game, with Paton rushing for 89 yards and Aldrich recording 14 tackles in the South's 17-0 win. Boylston then resigned for Pinewood Prep after a 41-17 five-year run, and St. Andrew's hired Karl DeMasi in January to lead football, baseball and eventually boys basketball.

Paton later earned second-team All-Coastal Empire honors at running back after his 1,784-yard, 20-touchdown season, while Zach Hillard and Matt Hunt were honorable mention linebackers.

SeasonRecap:
Karl Demasi's first St. Andrew's football team spent most of the 2000 season living on narrow margins. The Saints opened with three home losses by a combined 16 points, started 0-7, then won three straight SCISA AA Region II games to grab the league's third playoff spot before falling at Williamsburg Academy in the first round.

The early schedule was unforgiving. Hilton Head Prep edged St. Andrew's 9-7 in the opener, Memorial Day blocked a potential game-winning field goal to win 14-12, and Byrnes Academy held the Saints to one long Ryan Stratz touchdown catch in an 18-6 result. Thomas Heyward, First Baptist, Dorchester, and Calhoun followed before the Saints broke through in October.

The turnaround began with a 36-6 win over Sea Island, when St. Andrew's held the visitors to six total offensive yards and got touchdowns from Zack Hillard, Justin Dixon, Jeff Smith, Cam Aldrich, and Adam Ciccio. A week later, Hillard caught Jeff Smith's two-point conversion pass in the fourth quarter to beat Colleton Prep 22-21, with Smith rushing for 237 yards and two touchdowns.

Homecoming against Pinewood Prep clinched the playoff berth. St. Andrew's scored three touchdowns in its first eight offensive plays, forced seven turnovers, and won 24-16. Hillard's 12 tackles pushed him past his own school single-season tackle record, while Smith intercepted three passes. The Saints finished 3-8 after Williamsburg won the playoff opener, but the recovered archive now shows the complete 11-game path and the individual stat highlights that made the late-season run possible.

The recovered Savannah Morning News articles fill in all 11 results, including a First Baptist forfeit and the two-game playoff finish.

Adam Ciccio became the season's statistical engine. He ran for 909 yards and 14 rushing touchdowns, scored 15 total touchdowns, earned multiple City Player of the Week mentions, and joined Zack Hillard, Davy Clay, Matt Hunt, Billy McCarthy, Jake Smith, and Jeff Smith on the all-region list. Region play was tighter: Dorchester shut out St. Andrew's in St. George, the Saints beat Calhoun Academy on homecoming, Colleton Prep won on Wilmington Island, and St. Andrew's answered with a 43-8 road win at Pinewood Prep behind five Ciccio touchdowns.

The postseason began with a 17-14 win at Pee Dee Academy, where Fred Kryner's 34-yard field goal made the difference and Ciccio and Hillard both topped 100 rushing yards. A week later, Dorchester scored three fourth-quarter touchdowns to beat St. Andrew's 28-7. The season still left a clear paper trail: Ciccio, Hillard, and Jake Smith were selected for the SCISA Senior All-Star Game, and seven Saints earned all-region recognition.

SeasonRecap:
St. Andrew's 2002 football season began in a storm of mud, turnovers and missed chances, but it became one of the program's most memorable playoff runs. First-year coach Kevin Kunst inherited a small roster and a team that, by his own preseason expectations, looked more likely to have a decent year and reach the first round than to play for a championship. Instead, the Saints finished 9-3, won SCISA AA Region II at 4-1 and pushed all the way to the SCISA Class AA state final at The Citadel.

The first hint of the team's identity came in the opener, even in defeat. Memorial Day beat St. Andrew's 10-7 in double overtime, but the Saints' defense kept them in a game played on a wet field and tied it late on Jeff Smith's 1-yard run. From there, the Saints found a gear. They overwhelmed Hilton Head Christian 48-0 behind Jeff Smith's two rushing touchdowns and Davy Clay's three-touchdown night, then blanked Hilton Head Prep 49-0 as Cam Aldrich scored three times, including two interception returns. The defense kept shaping the season a week later at Thomas Heyward, where Clay threw for a touchdown, intercepted a pass and watched Michael Shuford's late fumble end the Rebels' final threat in a 13-7 win.

The region race turned on a pair of very different October wins. At Calhoun Academy, Josh Smith kicked the first field goal of his career, a 27-yarder with 2:17 left, after Jeff Smith powered the late drive and finished with 141 yards and three touchdowns in a 22-20 victory. Ten days later, St. Andrew's buried King's Academy 59-0 with a 39-point first quarter that mixed offense, defense and special teams: Jason Victor opened the scoring, Jeff Smith ran for a touchdown, caught another and returned a punt for a score, Ben Robertson scored on a fumble return and Aldrich added an interception return. The Saints followed with a 34-0 region win at Hudgens Academy, rushing for 342 yards and holding Hudgens to 108 total yards as five different players scored.

Then came the result that gave the rest of the season its edge. Colleton Prep handed St. Andrew's a 47-17 region loss in Walterboro, building a 28-3 halftime lead and shutting down the Saints' running game. In the championship preview later that month, Kunst called that night "one big, black mark on our record," and the Saints carried the possibility of a rematch with them. They answered immediately in the regular-season finale, shutting out Holly Hill Academy 34-0. Jeff Smith rushed for 228 yards and two touchdowns, crossed the 1,000-yard mark and entered the playoffs as the offense's anchor.

The postseason showed how far the 25-man roster had come. Kunst later said the "25 guys have bought into the team concept," and the playoff results backed him up. In the first round, St. Andrew's used a balanced ground game to beat Pee Dee Academy 40-12, with Jeff Smith rushing for 117 yards and two touchdowns, Davy Clay throwing touchdown passes to both Smiths and Aldrich finishing the scoring with a fourth-quarter run. A week later at Williamsburg Academy, the Saints survived the kind of tense game that had slipped away in August. Trailing 9-8 late, Ben Robertson recovered a fumble at the Williamsburg 17, Jeff Smith scored from the 2 with 1:11 left and Michael McClean's interception sealed a 14-9 semifinal win.

That set up the rematch everyone around St. Andrew's had been chasing. Before the final, Kunst said, "This time we're ready for them." For a half, the Saints looked exactly that. William Chisolm's fumble recovery and Jeff Smith's 55-yard punt return helped create a second-quarter touchdown pass from Clay to Josh Smith, and St. Andrew's led Colleton Prep 7-6 at halftime. Colleton's deeper roster turned the game after the break, scoring twice in the third quarter for a 20-7 win, but the Saints left Charleston with a season that had already outgrown expectations: five shutouts, a region title, a state runner-up finish and a team identity built around defense, Jeff Smith's 1,241 rushing yards, Clay's playmaking and a roster that kept finding one more answer until the final Friday night.

SeasonRecap:
St. Andrew's 2003 football season had the hard edge of a team trying to follow a state championship run with a smaller, senior-led roster. The Saints finished 5-4, went 2-2 in SCISA AA Region II and reached the SCISA AA first round, but the season was defined as much by its close calls as its wins. The opener at Westside Stadium set the tone: St. Andrew's led Memorial Day in the second half, got a 40-yard field goal from Will Massey and nearly stole the game on the final snap when Davy Clay hit Josh Smith deep before Smith was tackled at the 2-yard line in a 20-16 loss.

The Saints answered by winning four straight. They handled Hilton Head Christian 27-6, then rolled past Hilton Head Prep 36-15 behind Beau Hinton's 133 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Clay added a rushing touchdown and a touchdown pass to Jacob Rauers, while Hunter Saussy contributed a safety. Two weeks later in Ridgeland, Hinton's 17-yard third-quarter touchdown gave St. Andrew's the lead for good and Clay's 1-yard sneak sealed a 19-13 win at Thomas Heyward.

The region opener against Calhoun became a defensive test. Massey's 30-yard field goal in the third quarter was the only scoring in a 3-0 St. Andrew's win, and Clay preserved the shutout by falling on a Calhoun fumble in the end zone. Hinton carried for 102 yards, Omar Glenn added 96 more, and the Saints moved to 4-1 overall and 1-0 in region play.

The middle of the region schedule was less forgiving. Dillon Christian beat St. Andrew's 32-7 despite a 51-yard touchdown run by Clay, and defending Class AA champion Colleton Prep leaned on 380 rushing yards in a 28-14 win over the Saints. Clay kept St. Andrew's throwing back into the game against Colleton, completing 25 of 38 passes for 250 yards and touchdowns to Josh Smith and Hunter Saussy, but the War Hawks controlled the ground game.

St. Andrew's responded with its cleanest night of the season at Holly Hill. Clay opened the scoring on a 3-yard run, then hit Josh Smith for a 15-yard touchdown. Smith added a 34-yard interception return, Beau Hinton scored twice, and Massey returned a fumble 35 yards as the Saints built a 34-0 halftime lead and finished a 41-0 shutout. In the first round against Robert E. Lee, Glenn broke loose for a 60-yard touchdown, Hinton scored from 15 yards out and Clay found Smith for a fourth-quarter touchdown, but the Saints came up one point short in a 21-20 loss. The final record did not match the previous year's state-final run, but the 2003 team still left a season built on grit, defense, Hinton's running, Clay's playmaking, Massey's kicking and a group of seniors who kept pushing games to the final possession.

SeasonRecap:
St. Andrew's 2004 football season was the hard reset after the Saints' 2003 playoff run. Bob Curley took over for Kevin Kunst with a roster that had lost 13 starters, leaving senior running back-linebacker Matt Knight, senior lineman David Stubbs and junior center-linebacker Jamie Cooper as the only returning starters from the previous year's team. The preseason questions were blunt: Curley needed eight or nine freshmen to play right away, had to settle a quarterback job after Russell DeMasi transferred, and was trying to make a small, inexperienced group competitive in SCISA AA Region III. Read Jim Thomas' 2004 Savannah Morning News football preview.

The season opened in Kingstree with Williamsburg Academy's 34-0 win, but the next week showed how close the Saints could get when the defense kept them in it. Memorial Day beat St. Andrew's 6-0 in a game defined by 41 combined penalties, cramps and missed chances. Don Keene had a 36-yard touchdown run erased by holding and missed a 32-yard field goal, but Curley still saw progress from a team that had gone from playing Williamsburg to a 7-0 halftime score to pushing Memorial through a one-score game.

September turned that optimism into a weekly test of depth. Dorchester Academy held St. Andrew's to 58 total yards in a 42-0 loss, Thomas Heyward scored 40 first-half points in Estill, Pinewood Prep held the Saints to 12 yards of offense in Summerville and Hilton Head Christian limited St. Andrew's to minus-10 total yards while scoring all its points before halftime. Hilton Head Prep then opened the region stretch with a 40-0 win, leaving the Saints still searching for their first points and trying to keep a young roster together through a schedule full of older, deeper SCISA opponents.

The final three weeks gave the season its clearest signs of offensive life. At First Baptist Christian, St. Andrew's was still blanked 49-0, but the Saints produced eight first downs and balanced 75 rushing yards with 70 passing yards. A week later in Walterboro, the scoreboard finally changed. Patrick Maleki caught a 13-yard touchdown pass and kicked the extra point, then Knight broke a 29-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter as St. Andrew's scored twice in a 48-14 loss to Colleton Prep. Knight led the Saints with 93 rushing yards, and St. Andrew's finished with 162 rushing yards against a Colleton team that piled up 419 on the ground.

Knight gave the Saints one more strong night in the finale at Dillon Christian, carrying 10 times for 100 yards and scoring on a 43-yard run in a 33-7 loss. St. Andrew's finished 0-10 and 0-4 in region play, scoring 21 points while allowing 383, but the year was also a full varsity education for the freshmen and sophomores Curley had been forced to lean on from August. The record captured the pain of the rebuild; the late touchdowns from Maleki and Knight, the Memorial Day near-miss and the experience gained by the underclassmen gave the next season something to build from.

SeasonRecap:
St. Andrew's entered Bob Curley's second season with a young roster, only three seniors and a clear goal after the winless 2004 campaign: improve every week and find a way back into the win column. Curley framed the season in August with a line that became the measure of the fall: "Every positive is a 100 percent improvement over last year." The Saints still had to live through a demanding SCISA AA Region III schedule, but 2005 did bring visible progress. They finished 1-9 overall and 0-4 in region play, scored more points than the year before and built the season around a small group of older leaders surrounded by younger players learning varsity football in real time.

The season began with a 41-0 loss to Williamsburg Academy, but even that opener showed where the Saints could compete. Garrett McCarthy led the defense with 10 tackles and an interception, while St. Andrew's tried to get its Pro-Set offense moving behind players like Frank Howard, Jeff Howard, Bubby Pavlo and Patrick Maleki. A week later, the breakthrough came at Memorial Day. Jim Kingston scooped up a fumble on the Matadors' opening possession and returned it 25 yards for a touchdown, McCarthy rushed for 116 yards and a 5-yard score, and Pavlo hit Maleki for a fourth-quarter touchdown pass in a 22-8 win. The Saints' 22 points that night topped their entire scoring total from the previous season, and it gave Curley his first victory as head coach.

The middle of the schedule was much rougher. Dorchester held St. Andrew's to minus-9 rushing yards in a 60-0 loss, and Thomas Heyward pulled away 64-7 despite the brightest special-teams play of the year, Javier Gutierrez's kickoff return touchdown. Pinewood Prep, Hilton Head Christian and Hilton Head Prep then overwhelmed the Saints in consecutive weeks, using quick starts and big plays to keep St. Andrew's from finding much offensive rhythm. Those results left the Saints at 1-6 entering the final stretch, but the season still kept revealing individual pieces for the program to build around: McCarthy's two-way work, Maleki's kicking and receiving, Kingston's defensive touchdown, Gutierrez's speed and a roster that leaned heavily on sophomores and freshmen.

October closed with three region losses, but St. Andrew's continued to get flashes from different players. Pavlo carried 13 times for 35 yards against First Baptist, Frank Howard led the Saints with 30 rushing yards against Colleton Prep, and Skip McGee closed the season with 34 rushing yards at Dillon Christian. The finale also gave St. Andrew's seven first downs and no fumbles, a small but meaningful sign for a team that had spent the year trying to clean up mistakes while often playing bigger, deeper opponents.

The final record was still hard, but the 2005 Saints were not simply another winless team trying to survive Friday nights. They ended the losing streak, found touchdowns on defense, offense and special teams, and gave a young roster a full season of varsity experience. In that sense, the year did what Curley had hoped in August: it moved the program forward, even if the scoreboard did not always show it quickly.

SeasonRecap:
St. Andrew's began the 2006 season with a major change on the sideline. After the Saints had gone 1-19 across the previous two seasons, the school hired the Savannah coaching icon Jack Miller to revive the football program. Miller arrived with a 50-year coaching career, 153 football wins and a Hall of Fame resume built across stops that included Savannah Christian, where his final team reached the GHSA Class AA playoffs in 2004.

The results improved immediately, even if the rebuild was still demanding. St. Andrew's finished 3-7 overall and 1-4 in SCISA AA Region II, tripling the program's win total from the year before and raising its scoring from 29 points in 2005 to 138 in 2006. The season still included difficult region nights against deeper opponents, but the Saints were more competitive and began to reset the program under Miller's direction.

The roster remained young, with a large sophomore group and only a handful of upperclassmen carrying the transition. Bubby Pavlo, Thomas Withers, Andrew Chapman, John Scuderi, Clay Crosby, Alex Lovell, Donald Doddsworth and other returners gave Miller a foundation, while freshmen and sophomores filled many of the two-way roles. The 3-7 record was not a finished product, but it marked the first clear step out of the low point of the 2004 and 2005 seasons.
